proves: a linear gradient runs the way its direction says, on both axes and at an angle that is not 45 degrees, in both of the forms a direction takes
checkable: 392x136 on white, eight 88x56 cells at x=8, 104, 200 and 296, the first row at y=8..63 and the second at y=72..127. The ramp is #f03c3c to #285ad2, so the BLUE channel read as (b - 0x3c) / (0xd2 - 0x3c) is how far along the ramp a pixel is: 0 at the first stop and 1 at the last. Sampled 2 pixels inside each corner and at the centre.
ours: 0deg TL 0.95 TR 0.95 BL 0.05 BR 0.05 mid 0.49. 90deg 0.03 0.97 0.03 0.97 mid 0.51. 180deg 0.05 0.05 0.95 0.95 mid 0.51. 270deg 0.97 0.03 0.97 0.03 mid 0.49. 30deg 0.51 0.96 0.04 0.49 mid 0.50. The between-span cell 0.03 0.89 0.20 1.00 mid 0.55; the between-short cell 0.07 1.00 0.59 1.00 mid 1.00, its ramp finished by the middle and everything past it holding the last stop. The control is 0.00 at all five points.
chrome: measured on the same directions: 0deg TL 0.97 TR 0.98 BL 0.03 BR 0.02 mid 0.49. 90deg 0.01 0.99 0.02 0.98 mid 0.50. 180deg 0.02 0.03 0.98 0.97 mid 0.50. 270deg 0.98 0.02 0.99 0.01 mid 0.49. 30deg 0.51 0.98 0.02 0.48 mid 0.50. Every one of the five agrees with ours in sign and in shape; the hundredths differ because the two probes inset their samples into boxes of different sizes.
why_0deg_is_its_own_cell: it pins the SIGN. Our scene measures clockwise from twelve o'clock and so does CSS, so 0 degrees runs upward - the first stop lands at the BOTTOM of the box. An implementation with the sign flipped would be perfectly self-consistent and wrong, and nothing in this suite proved the convention before this cell. Chrome's 0.97/0.98 at the top corners against 0.03/0.02 at the bottom is the reference; ours is 0.95/0.95 against 0.05/0.05.
why_not_45_degrees: the fixture this replaces drew one linear cell, at 45 degrees, in a square box - the single arrangement in which swapped axes look right, since the ramp is symmetric about the diagonal and the box is symmetric about it too. 30 degrees in an 88x56 cell is asymmetric in both.
the_between_form: LinearDirection::Between is v1's [x0, y0, x1, y1] and a different code path from an angle: it says where the ramp begins and ends rather than which way it runs. The third cell of the second row ends it at the middle of the box, which is the case an angle cannot express - past the last stop the colour holds, so that cell reads 1.00 across its whole right half. NO CSS SPELLING, so this and its neighbour are v1-or-us rather than Chrome-answerable.
status: measured from the committed image, and the five angle cells are confirmed against Chrome. The exact interpolated pixels are Skia's arithmetic and are not pinned; what is pinned is where along the ramp each corner sits.
